content:
I have built a tactic which extracts some information from the main goal and hypotheses. It constructs a new Expression s_seq and applies it to the main goal like this: 

    let mvarIds' ← goal.apply s_seq (term? := some m!"`{s_seq}`")
    Term.synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing
    replaceMainGoal mvarIds'

(this was copied from evalApplyLikeTactic).

Now, the tactic works and does what it is expected to do. Also, the infoview says Goals accomplished! and I get those two blue ticks in VSCode.

But when this tactic is in use, i get a logInfo on the lemma declaration (example, theorem ...), which says: 

PANIC at Lean.Expr.bindingBody! Lean.Expr:1020:23: binding expected
backtrace:
/home/user/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.28.0/lib/lean/libleanshared.so(+0xa1452be) [0x7f8cfe1452be]
/home/user/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.28.0/lib/lean/libleanshared.so(lean_panic_fn+0x1c) [0x7f8cfe14574c]
/home/user/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.28.0/lib/lean/libleanshared.so(l_Lean_Expr_bindingBody_x21___boxed+0x5e) [0x7f8cf6ebbdae]
/home/user/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.28.0/lib/lean/libleanshared.so(+0xa04a662) [0x7f8cfe04a662]
...

see

Now I am not sure, if it is a problem within Lean or am I doing something wrong?
Unfortunately it is very difficult to create a mwe because my project is quite big and I have no idea, what might cause this problem. I can try though.
It seems like the error comes from running a tactic that calls bindingBody! in some nested function
You can try searching for bindingBody! in your code base perhaps
Yeah I am currently trying to do so. But when this would fail somewhere in my code, the tactic should not execute should it?
Oh okay! That is good to know, thank you!

So I went through the code and logged every occurence of bindingBody! or commented it.
Every expression looks good, no _inhabitedExprDummy in sight but the log still remains.
I thought it might come from the delaboration but turning it off did not help.
No the panic is in evalTactic, i.e. it is during the execution of a tactic. Did you log the output of bindingBody!?
I am just wondering why the panic log appears on the lemma declaration and not on the tactic which might cause this panic

Panics get logged to through IO.eprintln which gets collected into a string buffer and put into an info message after command elaboration. Also notably, IO.eprintln doesn't have any way to supply position information so it just prints out the whole dump.
